title: The Poisson parameter np (hundredths)
source: S2 Ch2 theory S2-2.3 Quick check 1 (B(80,0.04), lambda=3.2)
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{B}({n|int}{,}{P|num2})\). What is the Poisson parameter of a suitable approximating distribution?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The Poisson parameter is n times p, which is {n|int} times {P|num2}.

contexts.stem: A batch of {n|int} items each has probability {P|num2} of being imperfect, independently. What is the Poisson parameter of a suitable approximating distribution for the number of imperfect items?
Write down the Poisson parameter used to approximate \(\mathrm{B}({n|int}{,}{P|num2})\).

title: 9709/73/M/J/18 Q1: Poisson approximation to B(75, 0.03)

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF, parts (i) and (ii). Later questions on the paper are omitted. Fully manual: (i) is a Poisson probability and (ii) is a justification. Official MS: Po(2.25) (B1), exp(-2.25) times (1 + 2.25 + 2.25 squared over 2) (M1), 0.609 to 3 s.f. (A1), special credit B1 for the exact binomial 0.608; (ii) mean 2.25 is less than 5 and n is large (B1). Independently, the Poisson probability is 0.609339..., which is 0.609 to 3 s.f.

stem:
A random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{B}(75,0.03)\).

(i) Use the Poisson approximation to the binomial distribution to calculate \(\mathrm{P}(X\lt 3)\).

(ii) Justify the use of the Poisson approximation.

steps.name: po
steps.note: Official MS: Po(2.25), stated or implied.

steps.name: form
steps.note: Official MS: the Poisson sum, any lambda, one end error allowed.

steps.name: val
steps.text_tex: The probability is \(0.609\) to 3 significant figures.

steps.name: just
steps.text_tex: Here \(n=75\) is large and the mean \(2.25\) is less than \(5\), so the Poisson approximation is suitable.
steps.note: Official MS: mu=2.25 which is less than 5, and n large.
